title: Implementation velocity and blockers — Weekly sync 2026-06-10
body:
Summary:
Weekly solutions + proservices sync focused on integration throughput, outstanding blockers for active customers, and a short health check of our canary rollouts. Meeting ran ~45 minutes. Action-orientation: prioritize next-deployment unblockers and short technical spikes to avoid repeated regressions on long-tail inputs.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (notes/lead)
- Miguel Herrera (solutions eng)
- Priya Nair (inference eng)
- Ben Carter (CS)
- Lena Cho (SRE)
- Josh Kim (product, partial)

Key numeric signals this week:
- Tickets closed across active integrations: 7 (down from 12 last week; backlog increased by 3)
- Avg lead time from ticket open -> dev PR: 2.8 days
- Canary success rate (token streams > 4k): 62% passing validation checks

Customer-by-customer notes:
1) Nimbus Health (onboarding)- Status: near completion but blocked on customer TLS cert rotation schedule and internal network ACLs.- Technical details: prefix caching warm-up shows 30% slower KV hit rate due to NVLINK topology mismatch in their on-prem cluster. Suspect mismatch between our shim and their driver version.- Risks: if TLS rotation slips >1 week, Nimbus will delay go-live.- Action items: Miguel to run a quick compatibility test matrix (PROSERV-421) and share results by EOD 6/12. Ben to confirm cert rotation window with Nimbus (owner: Ben, due 6/11).

2) AtlasPay (payments flow, dedicated)- Status: canary deployed to 10% of traffic; observed two schema validation regressions for the /generate/structured endpoint.- Technical details: regressions linked to updated schema in client contract — they started sending nested metadata arrays that our parser treats as single string fields; failing 422/serialization.- Decision: hold canary ramp until schema mismatch fixed. Pushback from product: want to keep canary to collect real usage signals. Compromise: maintain 2% traffic for logging-only (no cost-critical paths) while we patch parser.- Action items: Priya to prepare parser patch and unit tests (PR: infra #1423) by 6/14; Aisha to coordinate with AtlasPay PM for limited 2% logging-only flow (Ben to confirm).

3) BrightCart (retail pilot)- Status: stable but slow inference tail latency on sequences > 2k tokens.- Technical details: our kernel selection logic chose float16 tiling that underperforms on their sequence distribution; fallback to int8-quantized variant reduces latency but impacts token-quality for the recommendation model.- Risks: quality vs latency tradeoff might push BrightCart to consider alternative model variants.- Action items: run a quick A/B evaluation on quality metrics for quantized vs baseline by 6/18 (owner: Priya + Miguel). Put results in Confluence page and present next sync.

Cross-customer operational blockers:
- SSO / OAuth refresh token rotation caused two integration failures last week; root cause appears to be our token cache TTL mismatch and a race condition during refresh. Incident blamestack: SRE traced to token exp and simultaneous refresh attempts.- Internal infra: a scheduled upgrade to our model-serving driver on dedicated hosts introduced a subtle drop in KV cache reuse (PROSERV-434). Rolling back the driver patch fixed immediate regressions for two customers but we need a long-term mitigation.

Decisions made:
- Pause full canary ramp for AtlasPay until parser patch lands. Maintain 2% logging-only traffic.- Postpone Nimbus production cutover until after cert rotation window is confirmed.- Schedule a short (3-day) spike for kernel selector improvements focusing on long-sequence latency (Priya + Miguel) starting 6/13.

Open questions:
- Can SRE add a small synchronous guard on token refresh to eliminate races without major perf impact? (Lena to prototype 6/12)- Do we have sufficient test coverage for nested metadata arrays across our SDKs? If not, add contract tests (Aisha to raise ticket).

Action items (owner — due):
- Miguel: Compatibility matrix for Nimbus (PROSERV-421) — due 2026-06-12.
- Ben: Confirm Nimbus cert rotation window with customer — due 2026-06-11.
- Priya: Parser patch + tests for AtlasPay (GH #1423) — due 2026-06-14.
- Priya + Miguel: Quantized vs baseline A/B for BrightCart — due 2026-06-18.
- Lena: Prototype SSO refresh guard + perf measurement — due 2026-06-12.
- Aisha: Create contract-test ticket for nested metadata in SDKs — due 2026-06-13.

Notes / misc:
- Link to sprint board: https://jira.redwood.ai/secure/RapidBoard.jspa?rapidView=140- Small UX ask from Product: add a canary metrics widget to the console for per-route schema failures; product will scope out a wireframe next week.- Quick wins this week: fixed a logging misconfiguration that eliminated a noisy error from the AtlasPay canary logs (reduced log volume by ~18%).

Next sync:
- Tentatively 2026-06-17; focus will be on blocker resolution and canary ramp decisions. Please update Jira tickets before the meeting.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep emphasis on short spikes over sprawling refactors this sprint; customers need unblock timelines, not big rewrites.
- Document any driver-rollout learnings in infra postmortem so Dedicated customers have clearer upgrade windows.
